main_body: Japanese town-house facade: a large grey-blue tile roof with a ridge band, a cream plaster band with slit windows, a lower eave skirt, and a dark wooden lattice front with a central doorway and straw bundles at the base.
top_band: Rows 1-5, a light grey-blue ridge band (L 83-158) with corner finials. Below it the roof tiles run as vertical stripes (rows 6-30) in the same lightness family, with no step or front-edge line.
evidence: The whole piece is stacked flat bands seen face-on: ridge, roof drawn as vertical tile columns, cream wall, thin lower eave, lattice front. The ridge is a thin cap, and the roof tiles show no foreshortened slope surface, so no horizontal surface reads from above. The lower eave (rows 41-47) is a flat band with no visible top. The lattice and door are painted flat, with only dark slits and no inset depth. Unlike the references, which show roof slopes receding to a ridge, this is an architectural elevation with a hat.

style.evidence: The candidate has 33 distinct colours against 66 and 185 for the references, and a median of 7 colours per tile against 11 and 18. Its dark edge pixels are 72% neutral against 7-9% for the references, so the outline reads as a neutral near-black line, not a tinted material tone. The roof has a few steps and some tile stripe texture, but the lattice and plaster are simple repeated patterns. Flat-fill coverage is only 3%. Overall it looks flatter and more sticker-like than the references.
